questiontext.text:
Read the following research goal:

{@q_text@}

Which method of data collection is most appropriate for achieving this goal?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Most appropriate method: {@correct_text@}

Choose the method by matching the goal to what each method does best:

  • Observation: best when you need to record real behaviour as it naturally happens.
  • Interview: best for deep, detailed understanding from a few people.
  • Questionnaire: best for collecting standardised data quickly from many people.
  • Experimentation: best for testing cause and effect under controlled conditions.
  • Secondary Data Collection: best when the data you need already exists in records.

questiondescription.text:
Daniel Murunga

Methods of data collection: selecting the most appropriate method for a stated research goal.

Ben (STACK audit)

Students are given a randomised research goal and select the most appropriate data-collection method. Methods restricted to the five taught in the lesson; framing and scenarios are distinct from the 'Identifying data collection methods' question. Each wrong answer receives a diagnostic hint about what the correct method is best suited for.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

feedbackvariables.text: hint: if is(correct_text = "Observation") then "This goal needs you to record real behaviour as it naturally happens, without influencing it." elseif is(correct_text = "Interview") then "This goal needs deep, detailed understanding from just a few people, exploring their feelings." elseif is(correct_text = "Questionnaire") then "This goal needs standardised data collected quickly from a large number of people." elseif is(correct_text = "Experimentation") then "This goal needs you to test cause and effect by controlling conditions and changing one factor." else "This goal can be met using data that already exists in records collected by someone else.";

falsefeedback.text: Not quite. {@hint@} Which method fits that best?

qtest.description: A distractor selected: fires the F branch with the diagnostic hint.
